They used less seasoning (Miwon?) than other restaurants and used a lot of real meat to make the broth, so it had a clean, less greasy taste. The noodles were thin, but they were boiled just enough so they were still chewy, and there was enough sauce that I enjoyed eating them refreshingly with cilantro. I ordered shrimp naem as a set menu with rice noodles, and the shrimp meat was chewy and chewy inside the crispy but not greasy noodle, so it tasted like dim sum, and I liked it even more because it felt like it had been a long time since I had a delicious meal. reviews.author: Eunah Jew
reviews.text:
The most delicious thing is braised lamb ribs with potatoes. It got the moisture right! Even steamed potatoes are cooked just right. The meat and potatoes are soaked in the soaked lamb fat, so it tastes really good. The meat is thick and melts in your mouth. The liver is also amazingly well done. I really recommend the braised lamb ribs as the portions are generous.
I ordered Uzbek rag noodles because I personally missed Uyghur rag noodles, but it seems to be a completely different type of food. It tasted like eating raw noodles dipped in tomato soup. There wasn't a lot of noodles, so I ate them for soup. I also tried Kurosutamyeon, and it was closer to rag noodles, but it didn't seem to have any salt in it at all. It only tastes sour. In addition, it contains beef, onions, paprika, celery, garlic cloves, small vegetables, and green onions. But I was very disappointed, perhaps because I knew the taste of what I ate locally. The noodles are a bit chewy, the seasoning doesn't cut into them well, and the toppings don't have that hot taste.
The traditional Uzbek fried rice was a bit disappointing compared to the taste I had locally. It tastes more like cooking at home than from a wok. It's a bit disappointing in terms of oiliness and richness, and the seasoning is just right, but I think the flavor would be enhanced if raisins were added. The beef topping is plentiful, but a bit dry. I was satisfied with the way the carrots were roasted. It cooked very gently.
I was satisfied with the lamb soup! There were two large pieces of lamb, potatoes and carrots, everything was tender and the broth was good. The bread crumbs that came with it were generous in quantity, but a bit salty. Even when I ate it with soup, it was salty.
Yogurt is ordinary. Just a common taste that you can taste at the supermarket.
Olivier Salad: This is my first time trying it and it’s delicious. It's similar to egg salad, but it feels a bit more finely chopped. It also contains meat with a texture similar to beef jerky.
Beef Tomato Stew: The meat is very tough. It's three times more difficult than Jang Jo-ram's. The portion size is large, but I recommend it if you can’t eat chewy food.

reviews.author: MONGSANG Factory
reviews.text:
This is a branch of Potala Jongno branch. Noodles such as tukba, tentuk, and tukfry, or in Korean style, sujebi, are excellent. There are many good foods to go with alcohol.

People who have been to the Himalayas often come here looking for tukba, but they are often surprised to find out that it is Tibetan food after thinking it is Nepalese food. A representative example is Momo, a Tibetan dumpling. Although Nepalese people also enjoy eating it, dishes such as momos and samosas are actually Tibetan foods. Personally, I recommend the spicy stir-fried C-Momo.

There are many other things to recommend as snacks. A representative example is Seku. Chang, Tibetan makgeolli, is also unique. The original Chang's alcohol content is quite high, but here, the alcohol content was lowered to suit Koreans and a little acidity was added, like yogurt. Just being able to drink Chang is reason enough to come here.

It's great to go anytime, but it has a terrace so it's a great place for a gathering on a warm, sunny spring day. It is a place where exiled Tibetans risk their lives to run it, so it is a place where one step can be of great help.

reviews.author: YennaPPa (Luscious.K)
reviews.text:
#Changsin-dong #Everest

"The majesty of the head office"

I had the opportunity to visit the main branch of Everest, a famous Indian and Nepalese restaurant that was much missed in Yeongdeungpo.
Like the Yeongdeungpo branch, all the store employees are local.
There are many Indian and Nepalese restaurants near Changsin-dong, and there are quite a few locals, so the atmosphere is not like Korea.

I also ordered two curries, two types of naan, one piece of tandoori chicken, and momo, an Indian steamed dumpling.

What is different from the Yeongdeungpo branch is the difference in temperature between the naan and the curry.
Because it comes out much hotter, it feels like eating fresh food.
So the curry tastes even better.

Butter naan is really good.
Regular naan feels a bit dry, but I like the butter naan, which makes up for that drawback.

The tandoori is a little spicy, but it is not like the hard tandoori of Yeongdeungpo that is difficult to eat.
The red meat is very chewy and delicious, and the breast meat is a bit dry but still edible.
I brought the leftover meat home and made chicken quesadillas, which turned into real Mexican food thanks to the slightly spicy flavor and spices without being sweet.
The chicken quesadilla I ate at home was crazier than the tandoori I ate at a restaurant haha.

The most impressive one is Momo!
The meat has a mild Indian flavor, making it exotic and Korean at the same time.
The taste of the remaining momos increases even more when you eat them with cilantro at home.

Although it is different from the top tier in my opinion, the disappointing memories I had at the Yeongdeungpo branch were made up for at the main branch.

As expected, the main branch appears to be majestic.

PS: To finish, I tried imitating the mouthwash method of India and Nepal. It's fun, so pay the bill and try it when you leave.

Recommended Menu
- Chicken Macani, Chicken Tikka Masala, Mutton Masala
- Flutter Panir (Spinach Curry)ㆍEverest Special Curry
- Jjol momo, jaomien, naan types (curry fill)

The Nepalese set meal consists of a spicy and light curry, mung bean soup dal bhat, potato side dish Aludum, spicy spice snack poppers, and yogurt. Mix rice with curry and dal bhat, and mix with yogurt or tomato achar according to your preference. There was no particular taste, so I felt like my tastes and dislikes were a bit different.

* No parking
* Cooking without allergenic ingredients can be requested.
* Nepalese dessert experience available at the counter (fennel seeds, sugar cane?)

The fluttering funnier had a taste of a mix of spinach and cottage cheese. It was unique but delicious. The subtle spice complemented it and it wasn't plain. The amount was not enough for one woman to eat.

There were many people who ordered curry and tandoori, so I think I should have chosen that. Of all the Nepalese restaurants I've been to, this was the most disappointing.

Located on the second floor of the building opposite the entrance to Everest, the most famous Nepali food street restaurant.
Food is cheaper than Everest.
If Everest feels like a clean foreign restaurant in Itaewon, this feels like a local restaurant on the streets of Nepal.
It's a good choice if you don't like the hustle and bustle of Everest and the Korean paradise of countless tables.
There is also a Schwecha Mart in the basement.
Of course, the owner is a foreigner (Nepal or India) and speaks Korean well. They were kind and asked for recommendations on favorite Korean dishes if you weren't sure what to eat.

I ordered mango and banana for lassi (drink), but the banana was grated into fresh fruit and the mango was given syrup. Therefore, bananas are recommended.
I also ordered a samosa (fried dumpling), but it had potatoes and various types of beans inside and it smelled of spices.
It's not to the point of being uncomfortable, but has a unique Indian-like scent.
Tandoori chicken is sold in 2 pieces or 4 pieces.
I don't know anything special, it was just regular tandoori chicken.
I ordered two types of naan: plain and garlic.
I think one order would be enough for two people. The size is larger than expected.
Plain and garlic both delicious.
It was so delicious that I ate it all even though I was full.
I ordered chicken curry, and there were 5-6 pieces of chicken chunks, and it was delicious. (Butter chicken masala and mutton curry were also recommended as delicious.)

Some Indian restaurants are said to be good at making tandoori chicken and others doing curry.
I think this place is better at curry.
The downside is that not all dishes are served at once, but sequentially like a course meal.
Maybe that's why there was a bit of a wait in between.
I recommend eating the naan type and curry and ordering everything else to your taste.

A restaurant with a nice atmosphere hidden in the alley of Dongmyo,
I also went to Dongmyo Garage.
At first, I was a little confused about the location, but it was a place with a real alley feel, so my expectations rose as soon as I arrived. It has a hip yet comfortable atmosphere, making it an especially suitable date spot.

We ordered Life Cream Pasta, Detroit Pizza Blockbuster, and dark beer.
As the name suggests, I was very satisfied with the Life Cream Pasta. The cream sauce was soft and had a deep flavor without being greasy, so I enjoyed it until the end. It’s the cream pasta of my life!!!!

Detroit Pizza Blockbuster is a menu where you can enjoy three flavors at once. It had a thick square dough with plenty of toppings, so it was fun to have a different taste with each slice. It was crispy on the outside and moist on the inside, so it had a great texture.

The dark beer we ordered together had an impressive savory yet bitter taste, and went well with the pizza and creamy pasta as it balanced out the flavors well. There are a variety of alcoholic beverages, so it's great to enjoy a meal or a drink.

Above all, the atmosphere is so nice that it's perfect as a date restaurant in Dongmyo, and alcohol is included. The food was so delicious that I will definitely come back!!! This is a restaurant that only I want to know about.

reviews.author: riky
reviews.text:
I went to AMEX Bimague as a walk-in lunch.

Fortunately, even though I came as a walk-in, there was still room and I was able to enter.
I came in through the underground valet, but there was plenty of parking space, so I think it would be okay even if it wasn't the valet.

There is a set menu for lunch, and the portions are really large.
I was already full after eating bread and shrimp, so it was really hard to eat steak...

You can have coffee after a meal, but I started drinking coffee first as soon as I sat down, and it wasn't that bad.

It was a bit hot in the room, so I asked the surrounding tables to turn on the air conditioning a few times, but it didn't change much, so it seems like the air conditioning isn't working well. Other than that I was satisfied.

The inside of the restaurant looks spacious, but there is an open kitchen, so there aren't many seats. Rather, the inside has a view of Bangsan Market, and the entrance seems to be a bit better with a view of Dongdaemun.

They say it's one of the best steaks in Seoul... Well, the steak doesn't feel that special, it's just... it's delicious, so I don't think you'll come here thinking of Peter Luger or Wolfgang.

I paid with Bimague, and additional Bonvoy points can be accumulated manually, so please check once more when making payment.

It was an E-Land buffet famous for its cost-effectiveness, and it seems like it's been about a year since I've had it. They are splitting it into two categories, high-priced single items and regular buffets, but the Don Don branch has been open for a while, so the number of customers is okay. There are a lot of seats and there is no waiting. The quality of the food is many, but there are almost no attractive and cost-effective items. I think Sotetsu BST is better because they cook the food themselves and select the ingredients. Vanilla. Even ice cream uses less raw materials, so it doesn't taste like regular commercial ice cream, and all menu items only involve assembling, heating, pouring, and serving preprocessed items. It's different from the buffet at the hotel. I tried a variety of things, but it was a struggle and it wasn't all that delicious, so in terms of cost-effectiveness, it's not that good, but in terms of cost-effectiveness, I recommend lunch at a 3-4 star hotel like Sotetsu.

Located near Dongdaemun History and Culture Park Station
I went to the dessert mecca, Russian Cake.

I visited late on a Saturday evening.
Maybe it's because it's a place that's already well known by word of mouth.
There is a long wait for in-store dining
Unfortunately, I did takeout.

What I looked forward to the most after returning home
I tried Medovic Original Cake

Sweet and rich as soon as you open the package
The scent of honey spreads softly
My mouth was watering even before I ate it.

Sheets stacked tightly in layers are typical.
Chewy and sticky rather than fluffy like a cake
The texture was strong and it was very fun to chew.

Especially the cream sanded between sheets.
It's not too sweet as if it's a sour cream base.
Rich and slightly pleasant acidity
It perfectly balances the taste of honey.

When you take a bite, it melts in your mouth.
Softness and heavy sweetness on the tip of the tongue.
It immediately took away the disappointment of the long wait.

I really liked how soft it was.
Next time, Napoleon cake too
I want to try it

reviews.author: MENA KI
reviews.text: It is full of unique cakes baked by the owner from Russia. The price per piece is around 8,000 won, which may seem expensive, but it is also quite large. The signature menu item, Medovic Honey Cake, tasted very different from what I had imagined. I imagined it to taste as thick as the Malenka honey cake sold at regular cafes, but it tasted closer to a butter cake than that. Napoleon cake, another signature, was even more delicious. Another hero is meringue roll. To be honest, I've never been satisfied with a meringue dessert, but the meringue here didn't have any fishy smell, and the sweet cream inside was as sticky as Greek yogurt, so it went well with the light texture of the meringue. I am very willing to repurchase the meringue roll next time.

reviews.author: Jongmin Moon
reviews.text:
It's delicious, there are a lot of foreigners

The price is around 8,000 won, so it's not cheap, but I like it because the cake doesn't taste that common.
The Napoleon wasn't too sweet and it was fun to dig into the layers, and the meringue cake was good because the sweetness matched the texture of a meringue cookie. I also wanted to eat a 25cm big eclair, but I couldn’t eat it because there was no room in my stomach.
These days, there are a lot of Malenka cakes made at the factory in cafes, but the staff here all speak Russian, and I can see two or three people making them continuously through the store window, so I feel more trustworthy.

The personnel is extremely rude and neglecting. When I paid at the counter, the counter girl told me in Korean that the coffe will be served at the counter (I'm not sure about my understanding for 100%, since I'm studying Korean). After the payment, I took the tray with bakery to walk to my seat, but the counter girl all of sudden grabbed the tray from my hands rudely and with visible annoyance told me that the coffee will be served with the food. Her rough action left me speechless, cause I barely face this kind of behavior at the coffeeshops or bakery. I think she thought that there are so many foreigners and they will never express their dissatisfaction due to the language barrier. I was frustrated by this action and when my coffee was out I went to the counter and told the girl that she should not act impolite towards the client. And she was like "ah, yeah, yeah". This made me angry even more. I told her that she was supposed to apologize. And with fake smile she roughly apologized. I don't target everyone at the counter except that one particular girl. If somebody hates to work in the service area, they should not be there. What is supposed to be nice morning coffee turned to the frustration. I don't recommend this place to visit. At this place 80% of customers are foreigners and the this bakery getting their income mostly from foreigners. The owner or staff should remember it.

The staff's attitude was very rude and unfriendly. When paying at the checkout counter, the cashier said in Korean, “Coffee comes out at the counter,” but I wasn’t 100% sure because I was studying Korean. After paying, I was about to go to my seat with the tray containing the bread, but the employee suddenly roughly took the tray out of my hand and said with an annoyed expression, “Coffee will be served with the food.” The behavior was so rough and rude that I was speechless for a moment. It was almost my first time seeing an employee at a cafe or bakery show this kind of attitude.
They probably thought that since there were a lot of foreign customers, they wouldn't complain because of the language problem. I was really offended by that behavior. When the coffee came out, I went up to the counter and told her not to be so rude to customers, and she responded indifferently by saying, “Oh, yes, yes.” I got more angry at that attitude. So I told him I needed to apologize, and he forced a smile and apologized perfunctorily.
I'm not criticizing other employees, but I just want to talk about that particular employee's attitude. If you don't like the service industry, you shouldn't do it. What was supposed to be a fun morning coffee session turned into an unpleasant experience. 80% of the customers here seem to be foreigners, so this bakery probably makes most of its money from foreign customers. I hope the boss and employees remember this. This place is not recommended.

reviews.author: Son Joo-il (Cecil)
reviews.text:
Hyundai Card Culture Project 29 Tom Sachs Exhibition
"Space Program: Infinity" - a journey into infinite space
Exhibition Overview
Exhibition Name: Hyundai Card Culture Project 29 Tom Sachs Exhibition
Subtitle: Space Program: Infinity
Location: Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP) Art Hall 1
Period: April 25 - September 7, 2025
Number of works: Approximately 200 pieces from the ‘Space Program’ series

First impressions: the overwhelming scale of bricolage aesthetics

The moment you enter DDP Art Hall Building 1, Tom Sachs’ unique world view unfolds. It feels as if you have entered a huge workshop, completely different from the neatness of a typical white cube. The overwhelming sense of volume created by over 200 works immediately draws the viewer into the artist's universe.

The core of the work: The paradox of handmade work

The biggest charm of Tom Sachs lies in the ‘paradox of handcrafting.’ He reconstructs cutting-edge space technology from everyday materials such as foam core, plywood, and staples. Rather than NASA's elaborate spaceship, it expresses human dreams for space with a roughness that looks as if it were made at a local woodworking shop.

“ALWAYS BE KNOLLING” and the neat arrangement of work tools found throughout the exhibition hall clearly reveal the artist’s philosophy. We pursue perfection, but that perfection comes from human hands, not machines.

Highlight works

Rocket and spaceship models
The large rockets that form the center of the exhibition look like real spaceships from a distance, but when you get closer, traces of plywood, nails, and staples are clearly visible. This contrast gives a strange impression.

mission control center
A reproduction of Mission Control, reminiscent of the actual Houston Space Center, is designed so that visitors can experience it for themselves. The meeting of analog sensibilities and the digital era is interesting.

Tool Wall
The artist's trademark tool wall is not simply an array of work tools, but a complete sculpture in itself. Everything from the position of each tool to the shadows and labeling is a calculated art.

viewing point

1. The joy of observing details
The impression of seeing it from afar and the impression of seeing it up close are completely different. It is fun to look for traces of ‘incompleteness’ that the author intentionally left behind.

2. Experiential elements
It is not just an exhibition to ‘view’, but elements that visitors can participate in are placed throughout. In particular, mission control experience is essential.

3. Philosophical message
Through the work, one can read the author's critical perspective on technology fetishism in modern society. It makes me think about the modern meaning of the ‘DIY spirit’.

What was disappointing

Because it was such a popular exhibition, there were so many visitors on weekends that it was difficult to observe the works in detail.
There were some parts where it was difficult to understand the artist's intention due to the lack of explanations for some works.
The exhibition space was large and the route felt somewhat complicated.
Recommended viewing method

Recommended for viewing on weekday mornings (can be viewed quietly)
Secure at least 2 hours of time
Get close to the work and observe its details
Gain deeper understanding by participating in the docent program
Commemorative photos are required in areas where photography is permitted.

I am grateful to be able to meet author Tom Sachs and his unique world view on such a large scale in Korea. I think it is one of the best works among Hyundai Card's Culture Project series.

It was an opportunity to seriously consider the questions raised by modern art beyond a simple ‘pretty exhibition’. I am confident that this is an exhibition that everyone can enjoy in their own way, from children to adults, art beginners to enthusiasts.

I hope you don't miss this rare opportunity to experience Tom Sachs' world, which simultaneously captures human admiration for space and critical reflection on technology.
